items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: I got tied up with the band Booker, Al Travis. God bless him wherever he is.

ctx.x: But would you cut out and go ahead and find a book?

Sometimes, sometimes I had to leave and go two or three weeks in front of the band to get bookings. Because my band should have been the number one band in the nation. I got tied up with the band Booker, Al Travis. God bless him wherever he is. And, when he got to New York, I was listening in the office and the guy told him, I said, Well, I understand that you have the greatest band to come out to South Alley, so I hope you stay straight. I never paid too much attention to it. I was too young a fella. And my…
Yeah, you mentioned that that had to do with the breaking up of the band.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: And then finally this Al Travis that was the biggest crook in the world.

ctx.x: Yeah, you would deal with one man?

One man. How much territory? The man that first picked me up was Bernard Galway. And I had him, not only was his name, but Rabinowitz. And then finally this Al Travis that was the biggest crook in the world. And then the next biggest crook was this one that I picked up here, Chauncey Highland, on the revision of my band. Those were crooks. They weren't under bondage like the big companies are now. And the only major company that I went with that was under bonds was when I went to Joe Glazer. See, Glazer wanted me…

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1974-01-01
items.q: all Al Travis would have had to do was continue the bookers from Florida back into New York and we possibly would have gone into all of the major, major spots because he knew how to sell it.

ctx.x: Well it's funny, they could have made honest money.

They sure they could have made a bunch of, all Al Travis would have had to do was continue the bookers from Florida back into New York and we possibly would have gone into all of the major, major spots because he knew how to sell it. That is really weird to me, you know, that a man could be such a successful salesman. And he's so crooked and so no good. And if he leaves the few bucks that he would have been doing, he would have been doing it. He would have built that up into a repeat there. That's going to be a…

I'm interested in baseball a little bit. I don't know much about it, but you do. I've always been fascinated in talking to people. Like, I don't know if you know Mooney Martin or not, but he used to play baseball long before your time and he's a friend of Tom Albers, but he would tell me about the different teams, Algiers they had, and they had teams out in the country. items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: The Booking Age, it's like Al Travis, the biggest crook in the world.

ctx.x: Yeah, I might find somebody who could do it in some sort of special way.

Maybe so. But, I have a few of them. And then too, a lot of this stuff was stolen from me. The Booking Age, it's like Al Travis, the biggest crook in the world. Then comes Rabinowitz, another Jewish Booking Age. And this guy, Chauncey Hallin. These guys take my material and when they jump the gun, I never see them on my material and all that's gone. Which was a big loss to me. Pictures, stories, and things like that.
Well, I guess sometimes you'd get top billing and sometimes you wouldn't. Well, yeah. It was very.
